ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p44#3/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p44#3/r2.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p44#3/r2.claim: The date-stalk «ʿurjūn» is the stem from the cluster’s branches to its origin; al-Zajjāj derives the word from bending.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p44#3/r2.anchor: العرجون: عود العذق من بين الشمراخ إلى منبته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p66/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p66/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p66/r1.claim: The accusative القمر is the majority reading while some reciters raise it as a subject; قدرناه can mean that God measured its course or assigned its stations or light through them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p66/r1.anchor: وقرأ الحرميان، وأبو عمرو، وأبو جعفر، وابن محيصن، والحسن: بخلاف عنه. والقمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p67/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p67/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p67/r1.claim: The moon's body is dark and receives reflected sunlight like a polished mirror, explaining its movement against the sun's light-stations without requiring an omitted preposition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p67/r1.anchor: ولا يحتاج إلى حذف حرف الصفة، فإن جرم القمر مظلم، ينزل فيه النور لقبوله عكس ضياء الشمس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p67/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p67/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p67/r2.claim: The Arabs know 28 lunar stations: the moon occupies one each night from the month’s start to its twenty-eighth night, then travels for two nights when the month is short; they are also the stars used to name rain omens.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p67/r2.anchor: وهذه المنازل معروفة عند العرب، وهي ثمانية وعشرون منزلة، ينزل القمر كل ليلة في واحد منها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p67/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p67/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p67/r3.claim: At the end of its stations the moon thins, curves, and yellows like an old date-stalk; old is relative usage, not necessarily a full year, and custom determines it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p67/r3.anchor: فإذا كان في آخر منازله دق واستقوس واصفر، فشبه بالعرجون القديم من ثلاثة الأوجه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p67/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p67/r4.speaker: سليمان التيمي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p67/r4.claim: He reads العرجون with a kasra on the ʿayn and fatḥa on the jīm; the majority use two ḍammas, two dialect forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p67/r4.anchor: وقرأ سليمان التيمي: كالعرجون، بكسر العين وفتح الجيم والجمهور

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r2.claim: The cosmic signs in this passage call for gratitude whose necessary expression is monotheism, and they also entail a day of reward and punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r2.anchor: all these signs entail gratitude to God and the essential requirement of this gratitude is monotheism

SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r1.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r1.claim: They read القمر nominative as a subject; other readers use accusative with an implied verb by الاشتغال, and both parses are equally sound.
SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r1.anchor: فالرفع على الابتداء، والنصب بإضمار فعل على الاشتغال، والوجهان مستويان لتقدم جملة ذات وجهين،

SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r2.claim: Both cases are licensed by the preceding two-way clause والشمس تجري: compare with its opening for a nominal clause or ending for a verbal clause.
SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r2.anchor: لتقدم جملة ذات وجهين، وهي قوله: " والشمس تجري " فإن راعيت صدرها رفعت لتعطف جملة اسمية على مثلها

SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r3.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r3.claim: The author rejects al-Akhfash's restriction: four readers use accusative without a pronoun referring to الشمس; 55:7 also has accusative after 55:5.
SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r3.anchor: وبهذه الآية يبطل قول الأخفش: إنه لا يجوز النصب في الاسم إلا إذا كان في جملة الاشتغال ضمير يعود على الاسم

SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r4.claim: منازل may be the second object of قدرنا meaning made, a circumstantial ذا منازل, or adverbial for the moon's course through stations.
SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r4.anchor: قوله: " منازل " فيه أوجه، أحدها: أنه مفعول ثان؛ لأن " قدرنا " بمعنى صيرنا. الثاني: أنه حال

SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r5.claim: The date-cluster stalk runs from its little branches to its origin on the palm; the moon simile captures thinness, curvature, and yellow color. The preferred weight is فعلول with original نون; al-Zajjaj says نون is extra.
SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r5.anchor: والعرجون: عود العذق ما بين الشماريخ إلى منبته من النخلة. وهو تشبيه بديع، شبه به القمر في ثلاثة أشياء: دقته واستقواسه واصفراره.

SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r6.speaker: سليمان التيمي
SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r6.claim: Sulayman al-Taymi reads with kasra on عين and fatha on جيم, both dialect forms.
SAMIN-DURR:36:39/r6.anchor: وقرأ سليمان التيمي بكسر العين وفتح الجيم، وهما لغتان كالبزيون والبزيون.

ZAJJAJ:v4p286#2/r12.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p286#2/r12.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p286#2/r12.claim: القمر is read in the nominative or accusative.
ZAJJAJ:v4p286#2/r12.anchor: يقرأ بالرفع والنصب، فمن نصب فعلى

ZAJJAJ:v4p286#2/r13.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p286#2/r13.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p286#2/r13.claim: The accusative coordinates with an implied “We appointed”: “and We appointed the moon in phases.”
ZAJJAJ:v4p286#2/r13.anchor: يقرأ بالرفع والنصب، فمن نصب فعلى

ZAJJAJ:v4p286#2/r14.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p286#2/r14.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p286#2/r14.claim: The nominative can begin a new clause, with قدرناه as its predicate, or complete an implied “a sign for them.”
ZAJJAJ:v4p286#2/r14.anchor: والرفع على معنى وآية لهم القمر قدرناه.

ZAJJAJ:v4p286#2/r15.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p286#2/r15.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p286#2/r15.claim: The عرجون is the stalk of a date cluster; when old and dry it becomes thin and small, resembling the crescent at the end of the month or its first appearance.
ZAJJAJ:v4p286#2/r15.anchor: وحقيقة العرجون أنه العود الذي عليه العذق

ASAD-NOTES:36:37#n20/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:36:37#n20/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:36:37#n20/r1.claim: Urjan is the date-palm raceme; when old and dry it becomes slender and curved like a crescent.
ASAD-NOTES:36:37#n20/r1.anchor: the meaning of the noun 'urjan - the raceme of the date-palm, which, when old and dry, becomes slender and curves like a crescent

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p397/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p397/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p397/r3.claim: The moon is a second great sign, unable to govern itself; God has set its monthly phases until it returns to the appearance of an old palm twig.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p397/r3.anchor: It neither controls nor governs itself. God has ordained various phases through which it passes every month.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p397/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p397/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p397/r4.claim: Urjun is the branch bearing date clusters; as it dries, it takes the crescent's shape in the moon's initial and final phases.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p397/r4.anchor: These branches after drying up assume the same shape as the one a moon has in its initial and final phases.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p397/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p397/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p397/r5.claim: The comparison rebukes foolish moon worshippers: the object they worship repeatedly wanes to a dry, crooked palm twig.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p397/r5.anchor: This comparison is pointing to the fact that the state of the moon whom these foolish people worship

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, and Abū ʿAmr read al-qamar in the nominative.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو: والقمر* رفعا.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r2.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r2.claim: The remaining readers read al-qamar in the accusative.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r3.claim: The nominative supplies an omitted آية لهم, parallel to the night sign in 36:37; آية is the subject, لهم modifies the indefinite noun, and its predicate is omitted as in the visible world.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي: الرفع على قوله وآية لهم القمر قدرناه منازل، مثل قوله: وآية لهم الليل نسلخ منه النهار

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r4.claim: The clauses about the night and moon explain the sign, as لهم مغفرة explains a promise and للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين explains a bequest.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r4.anchor: والقمر قدرناه منازل: تفسير للآية، كما أن قوله: لهم مغفرة [المائدة/ 9] تفسير للوعد

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r5.claim: For the accusative, al-Fārisī reports Sībawayh’s analysis as a fronted object resumed by a pronoun, like زيدا ضربته, which he calls sound Arabic.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r5.anchor: ومن نصب فقد حمله سيبويه على: زيدا ضربته، قال: وهو عربي

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r6.claim: He also allows the accusative to attach to the preceding predicate نسلخ; Sībawayh permits analogous alternation, as in زيد ضربته and عمرو أكرمته or عمرا أكرمته.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p39/r6.anchor: ويجوز في نصبه وجه آخر، وهو أن تحمله على نسلخ الذي هو خبر المبتدأ على ما أجازه سيبويه من قولهم: زيد ضربته

QIRAAT-ER:36:39:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:36:39:2#1/r1.speaker: CE
QIRAAT-ER:36:39:2#1/r1.claim: The nominative wa-l-qamaru makes the moon the subject of a new nominal sentence, breaking dependence on the verb in 36:38 and creating a fresh declaration.
QIRAAT-ER:36:39:2#1/r1.anchor: CE, mutawatir: Nominative reading (wa-l-qamaru): moon becomes mubtadaʾ (subject) of a new nominal sentence

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p141#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p141#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p141#3/r1.claim: Qatada identifies the old crescent as a dry, curved date-palm stalk.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p141#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ كالعرجون القديم ﴾ قال هو عذق النخلة اليابس المنحني

ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r1.claim: He explains تقدير as making the moon's course or place of travel into stations, with the course understood as an omitted first object and stations as second.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r1.anchor: أي صيرنا مسيره أي محله الذي يسير فيه ( منازل ( فقدر بمعنى صير الناصب لمفعولين

ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan supplies the verbal noun سيره; the verb takes one object and منازل is adverbial.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r2.anchor: واختار أبو حيان تقدير مصدر مضاف وقدر متعد إلى واحد و ( منازل ) منصوب على الظرفية

ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r3.claim: Some take the omitted object to be lunar light, waxing and waning as the moon's sun-derived light changes with proximity and distance; Earth may eclipse it.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r3.anchor: وقدر بعضهم نورا أي قدرنا نوره في منازل فيزيد مقدار النور كل يوم في المنازل الإجتماعية

ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r4.claim: Al-Alusi says the light explanation is not certain, only more probable.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r4.anchor: والحق أنه لا قطع بذلك وليس هناك إلا غلبة الظن

ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r5.speaker: أبو السعود
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r5.claim: Other parses make stations a second object with omitted ذا, or one object after deleting له; Abu al-Suʿud prefers the latter.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r6.claim: The fronted accusative القمر is governed by an explanatory verb, قدرنا القمر قدرناه, emphasizing divine determination; the changed style suits reckoning the month by the moon.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r6.anchor: ونصب ( القمر ) بفعل يفسره المذكور أي وقدرنا القمر قدرناه وفي ذلك من الإعتناء بأمر التقدير ما فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r7.speaker: الحرميان وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر وابن محيصن والحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r7.claim: These readers, with al-Hasan differing in one transmission, read والقمر in the nominative; most parse it as subject plus predicate clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ الحرميان وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر وابن محيصن والحسن بخلاف عنه ( والقمر ) بالرفع قال غير واحد على الإبتداء

ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r8.claim: Al-Alusi allows the same parsing as the clause about the sun running its course.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r8.anchor: ويجوز فيما أرى أن يجري في التركيب ما جرى في قوله تعالى : ( والشمس تجري ) من الإعراب

ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r9.claim: Indian astronomers count twenty-seven stations because the moon completes the zodiac in twenty-seven and a third days, dropping the fraction as less than half by convention.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r9.anchor: وهي عند أهل الهند سبعة وعشرون لأن القمر يقطع فلك البوج في سبعة وعشرين يوم وثلث فحذفوا الثلث

ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r10.claim: Arabs and nomads count twenty-eight stations not by rounding the missing third upward, but to track the solar year and seasonal work as lunar years drift through seasons.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r10.anchor: وعند العرب وساكني البدو وثمانية وعشرون لا لأنهم تمموا الثلث واحدا كما قال بعضهم بل لأنه لما كانت سنوهم باعتبار الأهلة مختلفة الأوائل

ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r11.claim: They observed the moon's roughly thirty-day return to its solar position and brief disappearance at month-end, then divided its visible passage from first evening crescent to last morning sighting into twenty-eight parts.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r11.anchor: فوجدوه يعود إلى وضع له من الشمس في قريب من ثلاثين يوما ويختفي آخر الشهر لليلتين أو أقل أو أكثر فأسقطوا يومين

ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r12.claim: The stations divide the celestial circle into roughly twelve degrees and fifty-one minutes; each zodiacal sign spans two and a third stations.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r12.anchor: فقسموا دور الفلك عليه فكان كل قسم اثنتي عشرة درجة وإحدى وخمسين دقيقة تقريبا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r13.claim: They tracked the solar year through the stations, seeing the sun hide three at once: one in its rays, one in dawn brightness, and one in sunlight.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r13.anchor: ورصدوا ظهور المستتر بضياء الفجر ثم بشعاعها ثم بضياء الشفق فوجدوا الزمان بين كل ظهوري منزلتين ثلاثة عشر يوما تقريبا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r14.claim: They measured about thirteen days between appearances, totaling 364 days, and conventionally added one day at Ghafr to match the solar 365-day circuit.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p15#2/r14.anchor: فوجدوا الزمان بين كل ظهوري منزلتين ثلاثة عشر يوما تقريبا فأيام جميع المنازل تكون ثلثمائة وأربعة وستين

ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r1.claim: One or two more days may be needed for the twenty-eight-day cycle to end with the year and return to the first star; Ghafr receives a conventional extra day.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r1.anchor: وقد يحتاج إلى زيادة يومين ليكون انقضاء الثمانية والعشرين مع انقضاء السنة ويرجع الأمر إلى النجم الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r2.claim: Arabs marked the twenty-eight stations with visible stars near or aligned with the moon's path; the moon appears near one each night.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r2.anchor: أن العرب جعلت علامات الأقسام الثمانية والعشرين من الكواكب الظاهرة القريبة من المنطقة مما يقارب طريقة القمر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r3.claim: The named stars are aligned with true lunar stations, according to Ibn Abbas and others.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r3.anchor: وهذه الكواكب المسماة بالمنازل المسامتة للمنازل الحقيقية على ما روي عن ابن عباس وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r4.claim: Because the moon's speed varies, it may pass a station midway, remain across two nights, or appear between stations.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r4.anchor: وإذا أسرع القمر في سيره فقد يخلى منزلا في الوسط وإن أبطأ فقد يبقى ليلتين في منزل

ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r5.claim: The popular rule of fourteen visible and fourteen hidden stations with each rising one's opposite setting is false: stars are not equally spaced on one path, so visible counts may be sixteen or seventeen and hidden thirteen.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r5.anchor: وما يقال في الشهور إن الظاهر من المنازل في كل ليلة يكون أربعة عشر وكذا الخفي وأنه إذا طلع منزل غاب رقيبه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r6.claim: Al-Sharaṭān is the dual of sharṭ, sign: two bright third-magnitude stars on Aries' horns, three spans apart north to south, with a small star near the southern one.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r6.anchor: أولها الشرطان بفتح الشين والراء مثنى شرط بفتحتين وهي العلامة وهما كوكبان نيران من القدر الثالث على قرني الحمل

ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r7.claim: Arabs called the Sharaṭān signs because their setting marked rain and wind; a nearby bright northern star is identified as one by some, and the pair are also called al-Nātiḥ.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r7.anchor: سمت العرب الكل أشراطا لأنها بسقوطها علامات المطر والريح والقمر يحاذيهما

ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r8.claim: Al-Buṭayn, the diminutive, consists of three faint fifth-magnitude stars in a sharp triangle on Aries' thighs, a spear's length from Sharaṭān; the moon sometimes crosses it.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r8.anchor: ثم البطين تصغير وهو ثلاثة كواكب خفية من القدر الخامس على شكل مثلث حاد الزوايا على فخدي الحمل

ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r9.claim: Al-Thurayya is a diminutive from abundance and is also called al-Najm; commonly it is six stars in a fan-like cluster with an eastward handle and northern bend, or a grape cluster.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r9.anchor: ثم الثريا تصغير ثروى من الثراء وهو الكثرة ويسمى بالنجم وهو على المشهور عند المنجمين ستة كواكب مجتمعة كشكل مروحة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r10.claim: Al-Alusi names Aḥīḥah b. al-Jallāḥ or Qays b. al-Aslat as possible poets for the Pleiades comparison.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p16/r10.anchor: وعليه قول أحيحة بن الجلاح أو قيس بن الأسلت

ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r1.claim: A cited line pictures the Pleiades at dawn like a grape cluster; four observed fifth-magnitude stars lie on Taurus' rump or, in al-Kashf, Aries' tail, and the moon may eclipse them.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r1.anchor: وقد لاح في الصبح الثريا كما ترى كعنقود ملاحية حين نورا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r2.claim: Al-Dabaran, named because it follows the Pleiades, is a bright red first-magnitude star at the tip of the seven-star Indian figure and Taurus' eye.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r2.anchor: ثم الدبران بفتحتين سمي به لأنه دبر الثريا وخلفها وهو كوكب أحمر نير من القدر الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r3.claim: Al-Dabaran is also called al-Mijdah; nearby stars map Taurus' other eye, face, and muzzle, and some call it the Bull's heart.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r3.anchor: ويسمى المجدح وموقعه عين الثور والذي على طرفه الآخر من القدر الثالث على عينه الأخرى والثلاثة الباقية

ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r4.claim: Al-Haqʿa has three faint stars like the dots of thāʾ, a cloudy mark likened to a circle or white patch on a horse; also called al-Athāfī, it lies at Orion's head.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r4.anchor: ثم الهقعة بفتح الهاء وسكون القاف وفتح العين المهملة وهي ثلاثة كواكب خفية شبيهة بنقط الثاء

ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r5.claim: The moon aligns with al-Haqʿa without approaching closely.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r5.anchor: وهي على رأس الجبار المسمى بالجوزاء والقمر يحاذيها ولا يقاربها

ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r6.claim: Al-Hanʿa, with nūn, is two third- and fourth-magnitude stars likened to a brand on a horse's hollow neck; al-Kashf calls it Orion's left shoulder.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r6.anchor: ثم الهنعة بوزن الهقعة وثانيه نون وهي كوكبان من القدر الرابع والثالث شبهت بسمة في منخفض عنق الفرس

ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r7.claim: The moon passes by the two stars of al-Hanʿa.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r7.anchor: وفي الكشف هي منكب الجوزاء الأيسر والقمر يمر بهما

ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r8.claim: Al-Dhiraʿ is two bright second-magnitude stars over Gemini's heads, named the Lion's outstretched arm; its folded arm is Sirius with its companion, and the moon approaches the outstretched one.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r8.anchor: ثم الذراع وهما كوكبان أزهران من القدر الثاني على رأسي التوأمين يعنون بهما ذراع الأسد المبسوطة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r9.claim: Al-Nathra is the gap of the Lion's nose, formed by two faint fourth-magnitude stars and a cloudy Cancer patch; nearby stars are the two donkeys, with the patch between them called the manger.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r9.anchor: ثم النثرة وهي الفرجة بين الشاربين حيال وترة الأنف وهو أنف الأسد وهما كوكبان خفيان من الرابع

ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r10.claim: The moon approaches the two nearby donkeys and eclipses each.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r10.anchor: ويقربها كوكبان يسميان بالحمارين واللطخة التي بينهما بالمعلف تشبيها لها بالتبن وبمحظة الأسد

ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r11.claim: Al-Ṭarf has two small fourth-magnitude stars in front of the Lion's eyes and forepaw; the moon aligns with one and eclipses the other.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r11.anchor: ثم الطرف وهما كوكبان صغيران من الرابع أحدهما على رأس الأسد قدام عينيه والآخر قدام يده المقدمه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r12.claim: Al-Jabha is the Lion's forehead, four stars in a crooked line; its brightest southern star is the first-magnitude Heart of the Lion, also al-Maliki.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r12.anchor: ثم الجبهة ويعنون بها جبهة الأسد وهي أربعة كواكب على سطر فيه تعويج آخذ من الشمال إلى الجوب

ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r13.claim: The moon passes the Heart of the Lion and the star next to it.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r13.anchor: أعظمها على طرف السطر مما يلي الجنوب يسمى قلب الأسد لكونه في موضعه ويسمى الملكي أيضا وهو من القدر الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r14.claim: Al-Zubra has two bright stars behind al-Jabha on the Lion's mane or shoulder; Arab usage puts the zubra at its nape, while astronomers place it on the back.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r14.anchor: ثم الزبرة بضم الزاي وسكون الباء وهما كوكبان نيران على أثر الجبهة بينهما أرجح من ذراع

ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r15.claim: Al-Zubra's stars are third and second magnitude, and the moon aligns with them from the south.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r15.anchor: فزبرة الأسد شعره الذي عند الغضب في قفاه أجنبهما من الثالث وأشملهما من الثاني وتسمى ظهر الأسد

ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r16.claim: Al-Ṣarfa is a single star on the Lion's tail, also called its tail; it is named for cold turning away when it sets.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r16.anchor: ثم الصرفة وهو كوكب واحد على طريق ذنب الأسد يسمى ذنب الأسد والقمر يحاذيه من جهة الجنوب

ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r17.claim: Al-ʿAwwa is five third-magnitude stars shaped like an Arabic lām, running from Virgo's left shoulder to below her breast with two bending into an obtuse angle.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r17.anchor: ثم العواء يمد ويقصر والقصر أجود وهي خمسة كواكب من الثالث على هيئة لام الخط العربي

ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r18.claim: Al-ʿAwwa is explained as dogs howling after the Lion or cold, as a cold-chaser, or as referring to the group's bent shape.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r18.anchor: زعمت العرب أنها كلاب تعوي خلف الأسد ولذلك سميت العواء وقيل في ذلك كأنها تعوي في أثر البرد

ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r19.claim: Another etymology derives al-ʿAwwa from bending, because the group curves.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p17/r19.anchor: وقيل من عوى الشيء عطفه فلما فيها من الانعطاف سميت بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r1.claim: Al-Kashf calls al-ʿAwwa the lower part of a person; it is also said to be the Lion's hip, and the moon crosses it.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r1.anchor: وفي الكشف العوا سافلة الإنسان ويقال أنها ورك الأسد والقمر يخرقها

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r2.claim: Simak al-Aʿzal is a bright first-magnitude star on Virgo's left shoulder near the ecliptic; the moon passes it and may eclipse it.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r2.anchor: ثم السماك الأعزل وهو كوكب نير من الأول على كتف العذراء اليسرى قريب من المنطقة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r3.claim: Simak al-Ramih is opposite Simak al-Aʿzal but is not a mansion; it is named for a star before it like a spear, and Simak means elevated.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r3.anchor: ويقابل السماك الأعزل السماك الرامح وليس من المنازل وسمي رامحا لكوكب يقدمه كأنه رمحه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r4.claim: Al-Ghafr is usually three or sometimes two fourth-magnitude stars on Virgo's tail and hind leg in a crooked line; the moon passes south and may align with the northern one.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r4.anchor: ثم الغفر وهي ثلاثة كواكب من الرابع على ذيل العذراء ورجلها المؤخرة على سطر معوج حدبته إلى الشمال وقيل كوكبان

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r5.claim: Ghafr is a good mansion between the Lion and Scorpion, and is said to rise with prophets and righteous people.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r5.anchor: وهو منزل خير بعد عن شرين مقدم الأسد ومؤخر العقرب ويقال إنه طالع الأنبياء والصالحين

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r6.claim: Ghafr is named for covering and diminished light; some place its stars in Libra.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r6.anchor: وسميت غفرا لسترها ونقصان نورها وذكر بعضهم أنها من كواكب الميزان

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r7.claim: Al-Zubana consists of two bright second-magnitude stars on Libra's shoulders, separated north to south by about a spear's length.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18/r7.anchor: ثم الزبانا بالضم وآخره ألف وهما كوكبان نيران من الثاني متباعد في الشمال والجنوب بينهما قيد رمح

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r1.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r1.claim: Several authorities identify the two Zubana stars as the Scorpion's horns; the southern one may be eclipsed by the moon.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r1.anchor: وقال غير واحد هما قرنا العقرب قد يكسف جنوبيهما

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r2.claim: Al-Iklil is three faint fourth-magnitude stars across a curved north-south line, with two following; the moon passes all. Another account makes four stars at the Scorpion's head, named for a crown.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r2.anchor: ثم الإكليل وهي ثلاثة كواكب خفية معترضة من الشمال إلى الجنوب على سطر مقوس

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r3.claim: Al-Qalb is the red bright second-magnitude star in the middle of Scorpio's three body stars; neighbors are third-magnitude Niyāṭayn, and the moon crosses and eclipses it.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r3.anchor: ثم القلب وهو العقرب كوكب أحمر نير أوسط الثلاثة التي بدن العقرب على استقامة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r4.claim: Al-Shawla, the Scorpion's needle in the Hijaz, is two close bright second-magnitude stars at its tail tip; the moon aligns with them.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r4.anchor: ثم الشولة بفتح الشين المعجمة واللام وتسمى إبرة العقرب عند الحجازيين كوكبان من الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r5.claim: Al-Naʿāʾim is four third-magnitude Archer stars after Shawla, the incoming stars toward the Milky Way; the moon passes two and aligns with the others, and four nearby stars are the departing Naʿāʾim.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r5.anchor: ثم النعائم أربعة كواكب من الثالث على منحرف تابع للشولة وتسمى النعائم الواردة أي إلى المجرة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r6.claim: Their name likens the Archer stars to beams laid across a well.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r6.anchor: وكلها من صورة الرامي وسميت نعائم تشبيها بالخشبات التي تكون على البئر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r7.claim: Al-Balda is a round empty sky patch, likened to a fox's cleared den, a desert gap, or the space between eyebrows; it lies behind the Archer's headband stars.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r7.anchor: ثم البلدة وهي قطعة من السماء خالية من الكواكب مستديرة شبهت ببلدة الثعلب وهي ما يكنسه بذنبه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r8.claim: Saʿd al-Dhābiḥ is two stars on the Goat's horns, a span apart; the southern is third magnitude and a nearby small star is called the sheep or its place of slaughter.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r8.anchor: ثم سعد الذابح كوكبان على قرني الجدي بينهما قدر باع جنوبيهما من الثالث

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r9.claim: Saʿd Bulaʿ is two stars on the Water Bearer's left hand above the Goat; a nearby star seems swallowed, explaining the name, while al-Qamus connects it to Earth swallowing water.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r9.anchor: ثم سعد بلع كوكبان على كف ساكب الماء اليسري فوق ظهر الجدي بينهما قدر باع

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r10.claim: Al-Qamus links the name Saʿd Bulaʿ to the verse يا أرض ابلعي ماءك; the two stars lie on one path, one dim and one bright, as if one swallowed the other.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r10.anchor: وفي القاموس سعد بلع كزفر معرفة منزل للقمر طلع لما قال الله تعالى ( يا أرض ابلعي ماءك )

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r11.claim: One explanation says Saʿd Bulaʿ lacks Saʿd al-Dhābiḥ's sheep and seems to have swallowed it; the moon approaches its northern star without eclipsing it.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r11.anchor: وقيل : لأنه ليس له ما لسعد الذابح فكأنه بلغ شاته والقمر يقارب أجنبهما ولا يكسفه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r12.claim: Saʿd al-Suʿud is two or three stars on a curved north-south line, the southern at the Goat's tail; the northern is third magnitude and the moon nears the southern.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r12.anchor: ثم سعد السعود كوكبان وقيل : ثلاثة على خط مقوس بين الشمال والجنوب حدبته إلى المغرب

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r13.claim: It is called Saʿd al-Suʿud because its rising marks the beginning of livelihood and flourishing livestock.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r13.anchor: وسمي بذلك لأنه في وقت طلوعه ابتداء ما به يعيشون وتعيش مواشيهم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r14.claim: Saʿd al-Akhbiya has four third-magnitude Archer stars on the Water Bearer's right hand: three form a triangle and one sits inside; its name likens one to Saʿd and the other three to tents.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r14.anchor: ثم سعد الأخبية أربعة كواكب من الثالث ومن كواكب الرامي على يد ساكب الماء اليمنى ثلاثة على شكل مثلث

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r15.claim: Another explanation says it rises before warmth, bringing out hidden creatures; the moon approaches from the south.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r15.anchor: وقيل : لأنه يطلع قبل الدفء فيخرج من الهوام ما كان مختبئا والقمر يقاربها من ناحية الجنوب

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r16.claim: Al-Fargh al-Muqaddam has two bright second-magnitude stars a span apart, on the Winged Horse's back and shoulder; the moon passes at a distance.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r16.anchor: ثم الفزع المقدم ويقال الأعلى كوكبان نبران من الثاني بينهما قيد رمح أجنبهما على متن الفرس الأكبر المجنح

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r17.claim: Al-Fargh al-Muʾakhkhar has two bright second-magnitude stars a span apart, on the horse's wing and shared by its navel and Andromeda's head; Arabs liken four stars to a bucket spout because of seasonal rain.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r17.anchor: ثم الفرغ المؤخر كوكبان نيران من الثاني بينهما قيد رمح أيضا أجنبهما على جناح الفرس

ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r18.claim: Batn al-Hut, also al-Risha or the Fish's Heart, is a bright third-magnitude star on Andromeda, in the imagined belly of a great fish; the moon aligns without approaching.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p18#2/r18.anchor: ثم بطن الحوت ويقال له الرشاء بكسر الراء أي رشا الدلو وقلب الحوت أيضا كوكب نير من الثالث

ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r1.claim: Arabs call the first fourteen mansions, from Sharaṭān through Simak, northern or Syrian, and the rest, from Ghafr through Batn al-Hut, southern or Yemeni.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r1.anchor: هذه المنازل الثمانية والعشرين تسمى العرب الأربعة عشر الشمالية منها التي أولها الشرطان وآخرها السماك شامية والباقية منها

ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r2.claim: A mansion's exit from dawn light is called its rising; its opposite's setting at dawn is called its fall.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r2.anchor: وأنها تسمي خروج المنزل من ضياء الفجر طلوعه وغروب رقيبه وقت الصبح سقوطه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r3.speaker: القطب
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r3.claim: Al-Qutb says mansions rising in rainy seasons are anwaʾ; opposite stars rising outside rainy seasons are bawarih.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r3.anchor: والمنازل التي يكون طلوعها في مواسم المطر الأنواء ورقباؤها إذا طلعت في غير مواسم المطر البوارح قاله القطب

ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r4.speaker: الجوهري
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r4.claim: Al-Jawhari defines nawʾ as a mansion star setting west at dawn while its opposite rises east; the pattern lasts thirteen days, except Jabha's fourteen.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r4.anchor: قاله القطب وقاله الجوهري : النوء سقوط نجم من المنازل في المغرب مع الفجر وطلوع رقيبه من المشرق

ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r5.speaker: أبو عبيد
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r5.claim: Abu Ubayd says he had heard nawʾ meaning a star's setting only in this context.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r5.anchor: قال أبو عبيد : ولم يسمع في النوء أنه السقوط إلا في هذا الموضع

ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r6.speaker: الأصمعي
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r6.claim: Arabs attributed weather to the setting star; al-Asmaʿi says they instead attributed it to the rising star in its period of power.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r6.anchor: والعرب تضيف الأمطار والرياح والحر والبرد إلى الساقط منها وقال الأصمعي : إلى الطالع في سلطانه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r7.claim: Anwaʾ is the plural of nawʾ, with nuʾān also given as a dual like ʿabd and ʿabdan.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r7.anchor: والجمع أنواء ونوآن مثل عبد وعبدان

ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r8.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r8.claim: Al-Tibi cites al-Marzuki's schedule: Sharaṭān three days, Buṭayn three nights, Thurayya five, Dabaran three, and the other mansions have the listed spans; his copy has no Risha period.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r8.anchor: وذكر الطيبي عن المرزوقي أن نوء الشرطين ثلاثة أيام ونوء البطين ثلاثة ليال ونوء الثريا خمس ليال ونوء الدبران ثلاث ليال

ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r9.speaker: الطيبي عن المرزوقي
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r9.claim: The schedule gives Haqʿa six nights; Hanʿa is counted with Jawzaʾ, Dhiraʿ has none, Nathra seven, Taraf three, Jabha seven, Zubra four, Sarfa three, Awwa one, Simak four, and Ghafr three or one.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r9.anchor: ونوء الهقمة ست ليال ولا يذكرون نوأها إلا بنوء الجوزاء ونوء الهنعة لا يذكر أيضا وإنما يكون في أنواء الجوزاء والذراع لا نوء له

ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r10.speaker: الطيبي عن المرزوقي
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r10.claim: The schedule gives Zubana three, Iklil four, Qalb and Shawla three each, Naʿaim one, Balda three or one, Dhabiḥ one, the next Saʿd mansions and front Fargh three each, and rear Fargh four.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r10.anchor: وقيل ليلة الزبانا ثلاث والإكليل أربع والقلب ثلاث والشولة كذلك والنعائم ليلة والبلدة ثلاث

ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r11.speaker: الشافعي وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r11.claim: If someone means a mansion itself sends down rain by saying rain came by its star, that is disbelief; al-Shafiʿi and others say the speaker may be executed if unrepentant.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r11.anchor: إن أراد به أن النوء نزل بالماء فهو كفر والقائل كافر حلال دمه إن لم يتب كما نص عليه الشافعي وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r12.claim: The Rawda says belief that a mansion truly causes rain is apostasy; the sound view permits saying it is a divinely decreed cause, distinguished from attributing rain to the star itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r12.anchor: وفي الروضة من اعتقد أن النوء يمطر حقيقة كفر وصار مرتدا وإن أراد به أن النوء سبب ينزل الله تعالى به الماء

ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r13.speaker: ابن عبد البر
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r13.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr says the permissible causal phrasing is still ingratitude for God's favor and ignorance of His subtle wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p19/r13.anchor: لكن قال ابن عبد البر : هو وإن كان مباحا كفر بنعمة الله تعالى وجهل بلطيف حكمته

ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r2.speaker: اللغويون
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r2.claim: Lexicographers commonly reserve qamar for the moon after conjunction and separation, from roughly the third through the twenty-sixth night; at other times they call it hilāl.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r2.anchor: والمشهور عند اللغويين أنه بعد الإجتماع مع الشمس ومفارقته إياها لا يسمى قمرا إلا من ثلاث

ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers the common sense of qamar, the familiar celestial body throughout the month, especially because it is mentioned alongside the sun.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r3.anchor: ولعل الأظهر في الآية حمله على المعنى الأول وهو الشائع إذا ذكر مع الشمس

ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r4.claim: God assigned the familiar moon specific stations and distances through which it travels, descending station by station.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r4.anchor: أي قدرنا هذا الجرم المعروف منازل ومسافات مخصوصة فسار فيها ونزلها منزلة منزلة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r5.claim: The moon reaches the later part of its course, when it appears close to the sun.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r5.anchor: أي صار في أواخر سيره وقربه من الشمس في رأى العين

ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda identify the ʿurjūn as the palm-cluster stalk extending from the frond to its base; al-Ālūsī says this is the well-known explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r6.anchor: وروي ذلك عن الحسن وقتادة وعن ابن عباس أنه أصل العذق

ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to explain ʿurjūn as the base of the date cluster.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه أصل العذق وقيل الشمراخ

ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r8.claim: Another explanation takes ʿurjūn as the twig of the cluster that bears unripe dates; al-Ālūsī favors the first, more familiar explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r8.anchor: وقيل الشمراخ وهو ما عليه البسر من عيدان العذق والكباسة والمشهور الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r9.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r9.claim: Al-Zajjāj treats the nūn in ʿurjūn as extra, deriving its pattern as faʿlūn from the sense of bending and curvature.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r9.anchor: ونونه على ما حكي عن الزجاج زائدة فوزنه فعلون من الإنعراج وهو الإعوجاج والإنعطاف

ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r10.speaker: الراغب والسمين وصاحب القاموس
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r10.claim: Al-Rāghib, al-Samīn, and the author of al-Qāmūs instead consider the nūn original, giving the pattern faʿlūl.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r10.anchor: وذهب قوم واختاره الراغب والسمين وصاحب القاموس إلى أنها أصلية فوزنه فعلول

ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r11.speaker: سليمان التيمي
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r11.claim: Sulaymān al-Taymī reads ʿurjūn with ʿayn kasra, rāʾ sukūn, and jīm fatḥa, a dialectal form compared to bizyūn.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r11.anchor: وقرأ سليمان التيمي ( كالعرجون ) بكسر العين وسكون الراء وفتح الجيم وهي لغة فيه كالبزيون

ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r12.claim: Al-qadīm here means old or ancient: the palm stalk has dried after time has passed; the resemblance is in its yellowing, thinness, and curvature.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r12.anchor: أي العتيق الذي مر عليه زمان يبس فيه ووجه الشبه الإصفرار والدقة والإعوجاج

ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r13.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r13.claim: One reported usage sets a minimum of one year for qadīm, illustrated by a manumission condition freeing every slave of his that is qadīm.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r13.anchor: وقيل : أقل مدة القدم حول فلو قال رجل كل مملوك لي قديم فهو حر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r14.speaker: أبو الحسن الرضا
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r14.claim: A further report, transmitted by some Imāmīs from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā, gives six months as the minimum period of qadīm.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p20/r14.anchor: وحكاه بعض الإمامية عن أبي الحسن الرضا رضي الله تعالى عنه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p18#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p18#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأهل البصرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p18#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, and the Basrans read al-qamar nominative, coordinating it with the preceding verse's night.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p18#2/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع، وأهل البصرة: "القمر" برفع الراء لقوله: "وآية لهم الليل نسلخ منه النهار"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p18#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p18#2/r2.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p18#2/r2.claim: The other readers use the accusative, linking al-qamar to qaddarnāhu: We determined the moon.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p18#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بالنصب لقوله: "قدرناه" أي: قدرنا القمر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p18#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p18#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p18#2/r3.claim: At its last station the moon grows thin like an old date-cluster stalk, which dries, curves, and yellows.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p18#2/r3.anchor: فإذا قدم وعتق يبس وتقوس واصفر فشبه القمر في دقته وصفرته في آخر المنازل به.

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r1.claim: God determined the moon’s course, or its course through stages.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r1.anchor: قدرنا مسيره. { منازل } أو سيره في منازل

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r2.claim: The moon passes through 28 mansions, one each night without skipping or falling short; at its final station before conjunction it becomes thin and crooked.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r2.anchor: ينزل كل ليلة في واحد منها لا يتخطاه ولا يتقاصر عنه

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r3.claim: Bayḍāwī lists 28 mansions: Cancer, al-Buṭayn, Pleiades, al-Dabarān, al-Haqʿa, al-Hanʿa, al-Dhirāʿ, al-Nathra, al-Ṭarf, al-Jabha, al-Zubra, al-Ṣarfa, al-ʿAwwā, al-Simāk, al-Ghafr, al-Zubānā, al-Iklīl, al-Qalb, al-Shawla, al-Naʿāʾim, al-Balda, Saʿd al-Dhābiḥ, Saʿd Bulaʿ, Saʿd al-Suʿūd, Saʿd al-Akhbiya, Fargh al-Dalw al-Muqaddam, Fargh al-Dalw al-Muʾakhkhar, and al-Rishāʾ.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r3.anchor: وهي ثمانية وعشرون: السرطان، البطين، الثريا، الدبران، الهقعة

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r4.speaker: الكوفيون وابن عامر
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r4.claim: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read al-qamar in the accusative.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r4.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون وابن عامر { والقمر } بنصب الراء.

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r5.claim: An ʿurjūn is a bent palm shoot; the word is on faʿlūn from inʿirāj, curvature.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r5.anchor: كالشمراخ المعوج، فعلون من الانعراج وهو الاعوجاج

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r6.claim: Two vocalizations are dialect forms, like two forms of bizyūn.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r6.anchor: وقرىء { كالعرجون } وهما لغتان كالبزيون والبزيون.

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r7.claim: “Old” means aged; alternatively it means a thing on which a year or more has passed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:39/r7.anchor: القديم } العتيق وقيل ما مر عليه حول فصاعدا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r1.claim: The moon is presented after the sign of daytime as the corresponding sign of night.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r1.anchor: ولما ذكر آية النهار , أتبعها آية الليل

BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r2.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وروح عن يعقوب
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, Abu Amr, and Rawh from Yaqub read al-qamar in the nominative, yielding the sense that it runs toward its appointed place.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r2.anchor: ومعناه في قراءة ابن كثير ونافع وأبي عمرو وروح عن يعقوب بالرفع : يجري لمستقر له

BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r3.speaker: الباقون
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r3.claim: The other readers put al-qamar in the accusative, emphasizing the grandeur and speed of its course; it covers in a month what the sun covers in a year.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r3.anchor: ونصبه الباقون دلالة على عظمة هذا الجري لسرعته بقطعه في شهر ما تقطعه الشمس في سنة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r4.claim: God measured the moon's course through twenty-eight stations; it then disappears for two nights at month's completion or one night as the month wanes.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r4.anchor: أي قسناه قياسا عظيما أي قسنا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r5.speaker: أبو القاسم القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r5.claim: Al-Qushayri describes the moon moving away from the sun until full, then drawing near it and waning until it disappears.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r5.anchor: قال الأستاذ أبو القاسم القشيري : يبعد عن الشمس ولا يزال يتباعد

BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r6.claim: An ʿurjūn is the date-palm stalk from the bunch's branches to its tip, thin and curved as it projects from the palm.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r6.anchor: من النخل وهو عود العذق ما بين شماريخه إلى منتهاه وهو منتبه من النخلة دقيقا منحنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r7.claim: The noun ʿurjūn is on the faʿlūl pattern; lexicographers connect the verb ʿarjana with depicting palm stalks on cloth, while commentators derive it from ʿaraja, to bend.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r7.anchor: وهو فعلول ذكره أهل اللغة في النون

BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r8.claim: Old means weathered: a palm stalk becomes thin, bent, and yellow over time, matching the moon's reddish-yellow hue.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p263/r8.anchor: ولما كانت حمرته آخذة إلى صفرة

DURR-FULL:v7p57/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r4.claim: God sets the moon's stations and makes it wane until it resembles a date cluster.
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r4.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {والقمر قدرناه منازل} الآية قال: قدره الله منازل فجعل ينقص

DURR-FULL:v7p57/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās lists 28 lunar stations: the 14 Syrian names are al-Saraṭīn, al-Buṭayn, al-Thurayyā, al-Dabarān, al-Haqʿah, al-Hanʿah, al-Dhirāʿ, al-Nathrah, al-Ṭarf, al-Jabhah, al-Zubrah, al-Ṣarfah, al-ʿAwwāʾ, and al-Simāk.
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {والقمر قدرناه منازل حتى عاد كالعرجون القديم} قال: في ثمانية وعشرين منزلا ينزلها القمر في شهر

DURR-FULL:v7p57/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r6.claim: The 14 Yemeni stations are al-ʿAqrab, al-Zabābayn, al-Iklīl, al-Qalb, al-Shawlah, al-Naʿāʾim, al-Baldah, Saʿd al-Dhābiḥ, Saʿd Bulaʿ, Saʿd al-Suʿūd, Saʿd al-Akhbiyah, Muqaddam al-Dalw, Muʾakhkhar al-Dalw, and al-Ḥūt; after all 28, the moon returns to its old cluster as at the month's beginning.
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r6.anchor: والعقرب والزبابين والاكليل والقلب والشولة والنعائم والبلدة وسعد الذابح وسعد بلع

DURR-FULL:v7p57/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the old urjun as the old base of a date cluster.
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {كالعرجون القديم} يعني أصل العذق القديم

DURR-FULL:v7p57/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r8.claim: Mujāhid says the comparison is with a dried palm cluster.
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {كالعرجون القديم} قال: عرجون النخل اليابس

DURR-FULL:v7p57/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r9.claim: Qatādah describes the urjun as a dry, bent date cluster.
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r9.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {كالعرجون القديم} قال: هو عذق النخلة اليابس المنحني

DURR-FULL:v7p57/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r10.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan compares it to a date cluster that has aged and bent.
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r10.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله {كالعرجون القديم} قال: كعذق النخلة إذا قدم فانحنى

DURR-FULL:v7p57/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r11.speaker: الحسن بن الوليد
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Walīd reports a man freeing every old slave; Yaʿqūb ruled the phrase covered one who had been owned for a year.
DURR-FULL:v7p57/r11.anchor: عن الحسن بن الوليد قال: أعتق رجل كل غلام له عتيق قديم فسئل يعقوب

DURR-FULL:v7p58/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p58/r1.speaker: الحسن بن الوليد
DURR-FULL:v7p58/r1.claim: The report continues by citing the old date cluster as an instance of something that has lasted a year.
DURR-FULL:v7p58/r1.anchor: قال الله {حتى عاد كالعرجون القديم} وكان لسنة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3195/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3195/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3195/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the old curved cluster as the old base of a date cluster.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3195/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله ، عنهما في قوله : كالعرجون القديم يعني اصل العذق القديم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3195/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3195/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3195/r2.claim: Al-Hasan compares the moon to a date cluster that has aged and bent.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3195/r2.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله ، عنه في قوله : كالعرجون القديم قال : كعذق النخلة اذا قدم فانحنى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r1.claim: These signs establish God's power and His exclusive right to divinity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r1.anchor: هذه الآيات جعلها الله عز وجل أدلة على القدرة ووجوب الألوهية له

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r12.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو والحسن والأعرج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r12.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, al-Ḥasan, and al-Aʿraj read al-qamar in the nominative, coordinating a full clause with the clause about night.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r12.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو والحسن والأعرج «والقمر» بالرفع عطفا على قوله وآية لهم الليل عطف جملة على جملة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r13.claim: With the nominative reading, another parse makes āya an opening subject with an omitted predicate such as “in existence and observation,” followed by two explanatory clauses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r13.anchor: ويصح وجه آخر وهو أن يكون قوله وآية ابتداء وخبره محذوف، كأنه قال: في الوجود وفي المشاهدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r14.speaker: الباقون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r14.claim: The remaining readers put al-qamar in the accusative, with an implied verb explained by qaddarnāhu; Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn Muḥayṣin, and al-Ḥasan also read it this way, with variation from al-Ḥasan.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r14.anchor: وقرأ الباقون «والقمر قدرناه» بنصب «القمر» على إضمار فعل يفسره قدرناه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r15.claim: Manāzil is accusative as an adverbial expression.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r16.claim: The familiar Arab scheme has twenty-eight lunar stations, and, by their reckoning, the moon crosses slightly less than one each night.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r16.anchor: وهذه المنازل المعروفة عند العرب وهي ثمانية وعشرون منزلة يقطع القمر منها كل ليلة أقل من واحدة فيما يزعمون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r17.claim: The moon's return is its reappearance as a thin crescent.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r18.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r18.claim: Al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan explains the ʿurjūn as the palm stalk bearing date clusters; when old it bends and yellows like the crescent, as observation confirms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r18.anchor: وحينئذ يشبه «العرجون» وهو الغصن من النخلة الذي فيه شماريخ التمر فإنه ينحني ويصفر إذا قدم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r19.speaker: سليمان التيمي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r19.claim: Sulaymān al-Taymī reads ʿurjūn with a kasra on the ʿayn.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r20.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r20.claim: Al-qadīm means old, having lasted for a long time.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p453#4/r20.anchor: والقديم معناه العتيق الذي قد مر عليه زمن طويل

BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r1.claim: The accusative al-qamara is governed by an omitted verb explained by the explicit one, as in Zaydan ḍarabtuhu; the sense is that God appointed the moon.
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r1.anchor: بالنصب بإضمار فعل يفسره الظاهر كما في زيدا ضربته

BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r2.claim: The moon has twenty-eight stations divided among the twelve zodiac signs and passes through exactly one each night.
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r2.anchor: وهي ثمان وعشرون مقسومة على الاثني عشر برجا

BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r3.claim: At its final station the moon becomes thin and crescent-shaped, then is hidden for two nights in a thirty-day month or one in a twenty-nine-day month.
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r3.anchor: فإذا كان في آخر منازله دق واستقوس ويستتر ليلتين إن كان الشهر ثلاثين أو ليلة إن كان تسعة وعشرين

BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r4.claim: The Prophet fasted eight or nine Ramadans; five had twenty-nine days and the remainder had thirty.
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r4.anchor: وقد صام عليه السلام ثمانية أو تسعة رمضانات خمسة منها كانت تسعة وعشرين يوما والباقي ثلاثين

BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r5.claim: The authenticated report that the two festival months do not fall short means a twenty-nine-day month has the same merit as a thirty-day month.
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r5.anchor: والباقي ثلاثين وقد قال عليه السلام :

BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r6.claim: The Muslim community follows the Arabic lunar cycle, whose reckoning is based on months rather than the solar cycle's reckoning by days.
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r6.anchor: وقد صح أن دور هذه الأمة هو الدور القمري العربي الذي حسابه مبني على الشهر لا الدور الشمسي

BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r7.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r7.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh locates the comparison at the end of one month and start of the next, when the moon becomes thin, curved, and yellow.
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن الشيخ : حتى صار القمر في آخر الشهر وأول الشهر الثاني

BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r8.claim: ʿUrjūn is formed from inʿirāj, crookedness; it is the date-cluster stalk between the dates and its point of attachment to the palm.
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r8.anchor: فعلون من الانعراج وهو الاعوجاج وهو عود العذق ما بين شماريخه

BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r9.claim: The date cluster (ʿidhq, with kasra) corresponds to a grape cluster; the shamarīkh are the stalks bearing the unripe dates, and shamarīkh has variant plural forms.
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r9.anchor: والعذق بالكسر في النخل بمنزلة العنقود في الكرم

BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r10.claim: Aged stalks become thin, curved, and yellow; the moon resembles one in those three respects to an observer, though the moon itself is immense.
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r10.anchor: فإذا قدم وعتق دق وتقوس واصفر شبه به القمر في آخر الشهر في هذه الوجوه الثلاثة

BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r11.claim: Qadīm means old by customary usage without a fixed duration; some say it requires a year, as in the legal rule freeing a slave owned for a year under an oath.
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r11.anchor: فالقديم ما تقادم عهده بحكم العادة ولا يشترط في إطلاق لفظ القديم عليه مدة بعينها

BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r12.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r12.claim: A Kashf al-asrar account says the moon first had complete light, looked at itself with admiration, and Gabriel struck its face and removed the light, leaving visible marks.
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r12.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : (ازروى حكمت كفته اندكه زيادت ونقصان ماه

BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas is cited as saying the lunar marks are Gabriel's traces; the light was taken but the mark remained, bearing the testimony of divine oneness and messengership.
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r13.anchor: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما كفت آن خطهاكه برروى ماه مى بينيد نشان ر جبرائيل است

BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r14.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r14.claim: In the same account, the moon is excluded from the divine court, seeks angelic intercession, and is allowed to prostrate once monthly on the fourteenth night; its light waxes as it approaches and wanes as it recedes.
BURSEVI:v7p311#2/r14.anchor: ماه ازفرشتكان مدد خواست تا از بهروى شفاعت كردند

BURSEVI:v7p312/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p312/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p312/r1.claim: The sun represents a servant abiding in knowledge of God, whose illumination is constant and never eclipsed or veiled.
BURSEVI:v7p312/r1.anchor: وقيل شبيه الشمس عبد يكون ابدا في ضياء معرفته وهو صاحب تمكين غير متلون

BURSEVI:v7p312/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p312/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p312/r2.claim: The moon represents a servant of changing states: expansion may raise the seeker toward union, then contraction and lapse diminish the state until God restores and refines it toward perfection.
BURSEVI:v7p312/r2.anchor: وشبيه القمر عبد تكون أحواله في التنقل وهو صاحب تلوين له من البسط ما يرقيه

BURSEVI:v7p312/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p312/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p312/r3.claim: A couplet voices the seeker's repeated descent through stations of divine love, each of which bewilders minds.
BURSEVI:v7p312/r3.anchor: ما زلت أنزل من ودادك منزلا تتحير الألباب عند نزوله

BURSEVI:v7p312/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p312/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p312/r4.claim: Al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya identifies the moon with the heart, illuminated first by the spirit and then by witnessing God; its twenty-eight stations correspond to the Quran's letters.

BURSEVI:v7p312/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p312/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p312/r5.claim: The first fourteen heart-stations are intimacy, righteousness, repentance, steadfastness, communion, forbearance, sincerity, devotion, humility, compassion, nearness, safety, yearning, and truthfulness.
BURSEVI:v7p312/r5.anchor: وهذه أسماؤها الإلفة والبر والتوبة والثبات والجمعية والحلم والخلوص والديانة والذلة والرأفة والزلفة والسلامة والشوق والصدق

BURSEVI:v7p312/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p312/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p312/r6.claim: The remaining heart-stations are harm, quest, thirst, love, jealousy, chivalry, proximity, generosity, gentleness, nobility, light, sainthood, guidance, and certainty.
BURSEVI:v7p312/r6.anchor: والضرر والطلب والظمأ والعشق والغيرة والفتوة والقربة والكرم واللين والمروءة والنور والولاية والهداية واليقين

BURSEVI:v7p312/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p312/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p312/r7.claim: At its last station, the heart takes on Quranic character and clings to God's bond; the verse about worship until certainty marks the end of the stations of servitude.
BURSEVI:v7p312/r7.anchor: فإذا صار إلى آخر منازله فقد تخلق بخلق القرآن واعتصم بحبل الله

BURSEVI:v7p312/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p312/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v7p312/r8.claim: The saying addressed to a believer in Paradise, Read and ascend, is explained as reading the Quran and rising through degrees of nearness.
BURSEVI:v7p312/r8.anchor: ويقال للمؤمن في الجنة اقرأ وارق يعني اقرأ القرآن وارتق في مقامات القرب

BURSEVI:v7p312/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p312/r9.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p312/r9.claim: The heart's course begins in intimacy with God, proceeds through faith, good works, repentance, and steadfastness, and is illuminated until it becomes full; nearness to divine witnessing then erases its sense of self.
BURSEVI:v7p312/r9.anchor: فإذا ألف الحق تعالى في أول منزله ثم بر بالإيمان والعمل الصالح ثم تاب وتوجه إلى الحضرة

BURSEVI:v7p312/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p312/r10.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p312/r10.claim: The heart's disappearance into God is true spiritual poverty, exemplified by the Prophet's saying, Poverty is my pride.
BURSEVI:v7p312/r10.anchor: وهذا مقام الفقر الحقيقي الذي افتخر به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله

BURSEVI:v7p312/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p312/r11.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p312/r11.claim: On the Night Journey, the Prophet's approach to God's presence increased his poverty of being; God found him needy and enriched him by generosity.
BURSEVI:v7p312/r11.anchor: ازداد في فقره عن الوجود كما أخبر الله تعالى عنه بقوله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, and Abū ʿAmr read al-qamar in the nominative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو والقمر بالرفع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r2.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r2.claim: ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read al-qamar in the accusative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي والقمر بالنصب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the accusative by an implied “We have decreed”: “and the moon, We decreed it in stages.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج من قرأ بالنصب فالمعنى وقدرنا القمر قدرناه منازل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r4.claim: For the nominative, al-Zajjāj supplies “a sign for them is the moon,” or construes the moon as a subject with “We decreed it” as predicate.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r4.anchor: ومن قرأ بالرفع فالمعنى وآية لهم القمر قدرناه ويجوز أن يكون على الابتداء وقدرناه الخبر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r5.claim: The moon descends through twenty-eight stations from the beginning to the end of the month; these were named in Sūrat Yūnus.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r5.anchor: ومنازل القمر ثمانية وعشرون منزلا ينزلها من أول الشهر إلى آخره وقد سميناها في سورة يونس 5

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r6.claim: At its final station the moon grows thin like the old, dried stalk left on a date cluster after the offshoots are removed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r6.anchor: فاذا صار إلى آخر منازله دق فعاد كالعرجون وهو عود العذق الذي تركته الشماريخ فاذا جف وقدم يشبه الهلال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba says qadīm here means a year old, likening it to the moon on the last night it appears.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة والقديم هاهنا الذي قد أتى عليه حول شبه القمر آخر ليلة يطلع به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r8.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj derives the pattern of ʿurjūn from inclination or curvature.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r8.anchor: قال الزجاج وتقدير عرجون فعلون من الانعراج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r9.speaker: أبو مجلز وأبو رجاء والضحاك وعاصم الجحدري وابن السميفع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r9.claim: Abū Majliz, Abū Rajāʾ, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī, and Ibn al-Sumayfaʿ read ʿurjūn with kasra on the ʿayn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p19#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو مجلز وأبو رجاء والضحاك وعاصم الجحدري وابن السميفع ﴿ كالعرجون ﴾ بكسر العين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r3.claim: The moon's stations provide a way to track the months, just as the sun marks night and day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r3.anchor: جعلناه يسير سيرا آخر يستدل به على مضي الشهور، كما أن الشمس يعرف بها الليل والنهار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r4.claim: He links the lunar stations to the Qur'anic explanation that crescents set people's and pilgrimage dates, and teach the count of years and reckoning.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r4.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {يسألونك عن الأهلة قل هي مواقيت للناس والحج}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r5.claim: Sun and moon each have their own light and different courses; the sun shifts its rising and setting seasonally, changing day and night length, and rules the daytime.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r5.anchor: فجعل الشمس لها ضوء يخصها، والقمر (1) له نور يخصه، وفاوت بين سير هذه وهذا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r6.claim: The moon begins the month faint, waxes nightly to fullness on the fourteenth, then wanes until it resembles an old date stalk before renewal.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r6.anchor: ثم يزداد نورا في الليلة الثانية، ويرتفع (2) منزلة، ثم كلما ارتفع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the old curved stalk as the base of the date cluster.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وهو أصل العذق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r8.claim: Mujahid says the comparison is to a dried date stalk.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد: العرجون القديم: أي العذق اليابس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r9.claim: Arabs name successive three-night lunar phases ghurar, nafl, tis', ashr, biyd, dira', thulum, hanadis, da'adi', and mahaq; the white nights are bright, dira' begin dark, and mahaq mark disappearance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r9.anchor: والعرب تسمي كل ثلاث (4) ليال من الشهر باسم باعتبار القمر، فيسمون الثلاث الأول "غرر" واللواتي بعدها "نفل"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r10.speaker: أبو عبيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r10.claim: Abu Ubayd rejected the lunar phase names tis' and ashr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p577#2/r10.anchor: وكان أبو عبيد (7) ينكر التسع والعشر. كذا قال في كتاب "غريب المصنف"

JISHUMI:v8p5880/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5880/r6.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v8p5880/r6.claim: Nafi, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Yaqub read والقمر in the nominative.
JISHUMI:v8p5880/r6.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب: والقمر بالرفع

JISHUMI:v8p5880/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5880/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v8p5880/r7.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Ibn Amir, Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read والقمر in the accusative.
JISHUMI:v8p5880/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي بالنصب

JISHUMI:v8p5880/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5880/r8.speaker: أبو عبيد
JISHUMI:v8p5880/r8.claim: Abu Ubayd prefers the accusative because both the earlier phrase نسَلخ and the later قدرناه provide a verbal governor.
JISHUMI:v8p5880/r8.anchor: أما النصب اختاره أبو عبيد للفعل المتقدم عليه والمتأخر عنه، أما المتقدم فقوله: (نسلخ منه النهار)، والمتأخر قوله: (قدرناه)

JISHUMI:v8p5880/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5880/r9.speaker: أبو حاتم
JISHUMI:v8p5880/r9.claim: Abu Hatim prefers the nominative because the moon is distant from the verb and can be treated as the subject of a new clause.
JISHUMI:v8p5880/r9.anchor: وأما الرفع فاختاره أبو حاتم، ثم قال: لأنك تبعد الفعل عنه، فترفعه بالابتداء

JISHUMI:v1p500#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p500#2/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p500#2/r1.claim: Al-qadīm, al-awwal, and al-sābiq are near-synonyms; qadīm can mean something existing from time immemorial, opposite ḥadīth, and derives from precedence.
JISHUMI:v1p500#2/r1.anchor: والقديم والأول والسابق متقارب في المعنى، والقديم الموجود لم يزل، ونقيضه الحديث

JISHUMI:v1p500#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p500#2/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p500#2/r2.claim: In theologians’ convention, the name al-Qadīm is not applied to anything besides God.

JISHUMI:v1p500#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p500#2/r3.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p500#2/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī denies that qadīm may name something besides God in linguistic usage.
JISHUMI:v1p500#2/r3.anchor: وأما من حيث اللغة فقال أبو علي: لا

JISHUMI:v1p500#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p500#2/r4.speaker: أبو هاشم
JISHUMI:v1p500#2/r4.claim: Abū Hāshim allows qadīm to be applied to something besides God in linguistic usage.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p17/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p17/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p17/r7.claim: One possibility is nightly stations, waxing early in the month then waning to the start.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p17/r7.anchor: أحدهما : جعله في كل ليلة على مقر له , يزيد في كل ليلة من أول الشهر حتى يستكمل ثم ينقص بعد استكماله حتى يعود كما بدأ , وهو محتمل

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p17/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p17/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p17/r8.claim: Another view says it rises in a station nightly, completing stations monthly; some make a solar year thirteen lunar months.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p17/r8.anchor: الثاني : أنه يطلع كل ليلة في منزل حتى يستكمل جميع المنازل في كل شهر , ولذلك جعل بعض الحساب السنة الشمسية ثلاثة عشر شهرا قمريا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p17/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p17/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p17/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says the old arjun is a dried curved date cluster; al-Asha's poem is evidence.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p17/r9.anchor: أحدهما : أنه العذق اليابس إذا استقوس , وهو معنى قول ابن عباس , ومنه قول أعشى قيس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p17/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p17/r10.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p17/r10.claim: Al-Hasan says it means a bent palm tree.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p17/r10.anchor: الثاني : أنه النخل إذا انحنى مائلا , قاله الحسن

MUQATIL:36:38-40/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:38-40/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:38-40/r2.claim: The moon grows through its stations, reaches fullness, then wanes toward the month’s end.
MUQATIL:36:38-40/r2.anchor: فى السماء يزيد، ثم يستوى، ثم ينقص فى آخر الشهر

MUQATIL:36:38-40/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:38-40/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:38-40/r3.claim: The old arjun is a dried, curved date stalk a year old; the waning moon returns to a threadlike shape.
MUQATIL:36:38-40/r3.anchor: أول ما استهل فيه كالعرجون، يعنى العذق اليابس المنحنى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p9#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p9#2/r1.speaker: مكي ونافع وأبو عمرو وسهل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p9#2/r1.claim: They read al-qamar in the nominative, either as a subject whose predicate is qaddarnahu or as linked to wa-āyatun lahum al-qamar.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p9#2/r1.anchor: وبالرفع مكي ونافع وأبو عمرو وسهل على الابتداء والخبر قدرناه أو على وآية لهم القمر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p9#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p9#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p9#2/r2.claim: On the accusative reading, al-qamar is governed by an implied verb explained by qaddarnahu.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p9#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p9#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p9#2/r3.claim: The moon has 28 stations, passing one per night without skipping or falling short; it traverses them from the first crescent night through the 28th, then disappears for one or two nights depending on the month's length.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p9#2/r3.anchor: وهى ثمانية وعشرون منزلا لا ينزل القمر كل ليلة فى واحد منها لا يتخطاه ولا يتقاصر عنه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p9#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p9#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p9#2/r4.claim: The phrase requires an understood noun: God measured either the moon's light, which waxes and wanes, or its course, with the stations functioning adverbially.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p9#2/r4.anchor: ولابد فى قدرناه منازل من تقدير مضاف لأنه لا معنى لتقدير نفس القمر منازل أي قدرنا نوره

NASAFI-FULL:v4p9#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p9#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p9#2/r5.claim: Al-ʿurjūn is the dried, curved date-cluster stalk, named from bending; al-qadīm means weathered. The moon resembles it in thinness, curvature, and yellowness.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p9#2/r5.anchor: هو عود الشمراخ إذا يبس واعوج ووزنه فعلون من الانعراج وهو الانعطاف

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r1.claim: Wa al-qamar can mean ‘and a sign for them is the moon,’ or qamar can be a nominative subject.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r1.anchor: يكون تقديره وآية لهم القمر. ويجوز أن يكون

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r2.speaker: الكوفيون وأبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r2.claim: The Kufans read qamar accusative by an implied verb; Abu ʿUbayd chooses it because verbs precede and follow.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r2.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون «والقمر» بالنصب على إضمار فعل وهو اختيار أبي عبيد.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r3.speaker: النحاس والفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r3.claim: Al-Nahhas reports grammarians favor nominative; al-Farra prefers coordination with the previous sign and sun.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r3.anchor: النحاس: وأهل العربية جميعا فيما علمت على خلاف ما قال، منهم الفراء قال: الرفع أعجب إلي

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r4.speaker: أبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r4.claim: Abu Hatim prefers nominative because the verb is occupied by its object pronoun.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r4.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: الرفع أولى لأنك شغلت الفعل عنه بالضمير

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r5.claim: Two parses: made it possess mansions (12:82), or appointed mansions for it with omitted lām (7:155).
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r5.anchor: ففي هذا جوابان: أحدهما قدرناه ذا منازل مثل

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r6.claim: First ten mansions: الشرطان، البطين، الثريا، الدبران، الهقعة، الهنعة، الذراع، النثرة، الطرف، الجبهة.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r6.anchor: وهي: الشرطان. البطين. الثريا. الدبران. الهقعة. الهنعة. الذراع. النثرة. الطرف. الجبهة.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r7.claim: Next ten: الخرتان، الصرفة، العواء، السماك، الغفر، الزبانيان، الإكليل، القلب، الشولة، النعائم.
