QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r7.anchor: الخراتان. الصرفة. العواء. السماك. الغفر. الزبانيان. الإكليل. القلب. الشولة. النعائم.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r8.claim: Final eight: البلدة، سعد الذابح، سعد بلع، سعد السعود، سعد الأخبية، الفرغ المقدم، الفرغ المؤخر، بطن الحوت.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r8.anchor: البلدة. سعد الذابح. سعد بلع. سعد السعود. سعد الأخبية. الفرغ المقدم. الفرغ المؤخر. بطن الحوت.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r9.claim: The moon cycles through 28 mansions, disappears, then starts again; each zodiac sign has two mansions and a third.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r9.anchor: فإذا صار القمر في آخرها عاد إلى أولها، فيقطع الفلك في ثمان وعشرين ليلة.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r10.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r10.claim: A cosmology says sun and moon were fire clothed with light; sunlight comes from the Throne, moonlight from the Kursi, and Gabriel’s wing erased moonlight.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r10.anchor: وقيل: إن الله تعالى خلق الشمس والقمر من نار ثم كسيا النور عند الطلوع، فأما نور الشمس فمن نور العرش

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r11.claim: The account puts the moon in a water casing and course: it waxes to fullness, then wanes from the side unseen by the sun.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39/r11.anchor: ثم جعل في غلاف من ماء، ثم جعل له مجرى، فكل ليلة يبدو للخلق

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r1.claim: Qamar is named because its brightness whitens the sky until it disappears.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r1.anchor: لأنه يقمر أي يبيض الجو ببياضه

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines urjun as the date-cluster stalk; its name derives from bending, with n added.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج: هو عود العذق الذي عليه الشماريخ، وهو فعلون من الانعراج وهو الانعطاف

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r3.claim: Qatada calls it the dry, bent date cluster.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو العذق اليابس المنحني من النخلة.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r4.speaker: ثعلب
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r4.claim: Thaʿlab says it is the date-cluster base left after cutting; qadim means worn out.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r4.anchor: ثعلب: «كالعرجون القديم» قال: «العرجون» الذي يبقى من الكباسة في النخلة إذا قطعت

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r5.speaker: الخليل
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r5.claim: Al-Khalil defines it as the broad yellow base of a date cluster, like a curved crescent.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r5.anchor: الخليل: في باب الرباعي «العرجون» أصل العذق وهو أصفر عريض يشبه به الهلال

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r6.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r6.claim: Al-Jawhari says it is the bent base left dry after date stems are cut; n is original.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r6.anchor: الجوهري: «العرجون» أصل العذق الذي يعوج وتقطع منه الشماريخ

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r7.speaker: الأعشى بن قيس
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r7.claim: Al-Aʿsha ibn Qays compares the yellow moon to an urjun.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#2/r7.anchor: ومنه شعر أعشى بني قيس: شرق المسك والعبير بها فهي صفراء كعرجون القمر

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r1.claim: An aged, dried, curved stalk resembles the moon in thinness and yellow color.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r1.anchor: فالعرجون إذا عتق ويبس وتقوس شبه القمر في دقته وصفرته به.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r2.claim: Other names include al-ihan, al-kabasa, al-qinw; Egyptians call it al-isbata.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r2.anchor: ويقال له أيضا الإهان والكباسة والقنو، وأهل مصر يسمونه الإسباطة.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari gives al-urjun on al-furjun’s pattern as a variant, meaning the stalk between palm branches and base.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r3.anchor: وقرىء: «العرجون» بوزن الفرجون وهما لغتان كالبزيون والبزيون ذكره الزمخشري

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r4.claim: Spring begins 15 Adhar, lasts 92 days, and crosses Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and seven listed mansions.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r4.anchor: فأولها الربيع، وأوله خمسة عشر يوما من أذار، وعدد أيامه اثنان وتسعون يوما

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r5.claim: Summer begins 15 Haziran, lasts 92 days, and crosses Cancer, Leo, Virgo, and seven mansions.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r5.anchor: ثم يدخل فصل الصيف في خمسة عشر يوما من حزيران، وعدد أيامه اثنان وتسعون يوما

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r6.claim: Autumn begins 15 Aylul, lasts 91 days, and crosses Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, and seven mansions.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r6.anchor: ثم يدخل فصل الخريف في خمسة عشر يوما من أيلول، وعدد أيامه أحد وتسعون يوما

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r7.claim: Winter begins 15 Kanun I, lasts 90 or sometimes 91 days, and crosses Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces, and seven mansions.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r7.anchor: ثم يدخل فصل الشتاء في خمسة عشر يوما من كانون الأول، وعدد أيامه تسعون يوما وربما كان أحدا وتسعين

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r8.claim: Most Syriac months have 31 days, four have 30, and Shubat has 28¼.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r8.anchor: وهذه قسمة السريانيين لشهورها: تشرين الأول، تشرين الثاني، كانون الأول، كانون الثاني، أشباط، آذار

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r9.claim: The account prompts contemplation of God’s power.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r9.anchor: وإنما أردنا بهذا أن تنظر في قدرة الله تعالى فذلك قوله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r10.claim: The moon is one station after the sun and dawn two before; it advances nightly through 28, then rises after the sun’s station.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r10.anchor: فإذا كانت الشمس في منزل أهل الهلال بالمنزل الذي بعده، وكان الفجر بمنزلتين من قبله

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r11.claim: Zamakhshari glosses qadim as worn or changed: the stalk thins, bends, and yellows, resembling the moon three ways.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r11.anchor: قال الزمخشري: القديم المحول وإذا قدم دق وانحنى واصفر فشبه القمر به من ثلاثة أوجه

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r12.claim: In legal usage qadim can mean a year; a declaration or will freeing old slaves frees those held a year or more.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r12.anchor: فلو أن رجلا قال: كل مملوك لي قديم فهو حر، أو كتب ذلك في وصيته عتق من مضى له حول

QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r13.claim: He refers to al-Baqara for rulings derived from lunar crescents.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:39#3/r13.anchor: قد مضى في «البقرة» ما يترتب على الأهلة من الأحكام

QASHANI:36:37-39/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:36:37-39/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:36:37-39/r3.claim: The moon symbolizes the heart, whose course passes through stations such as fear, hope, patience, gratitude, trust, and contentment.
QASHANI:36:37-39/r3.anchor: قدرنا مسيره في سيره { منازل } من الخوف والرجاء والصبر والشكر

QASHANI:36:37-39/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:36:37-39/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:36:37-39/r4.claim: The old curved palm stalk represents the heart as it approaches absorption in the spirit at the station of the secret, its face toward the spirit illuminated before its full annihilation there.
QASHANI:36:37-39/r4.anchor: عند فنائه في الروح في مقام السر

QASHANI:36:37-39/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:36:37-39/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:36:37-39/r5.claim: The heart's luminosity veils it from the soul and faculties; it is full when situated in the breast facing the station of the secret.

STUDYQURAN:36:39/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:39/r1.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:36:39/r1.claim: Q explains the lunar mansions as the Moon’s waxing and waning through twenty-eight stations during one lunar month.

STUDYQURAN:36:39/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:39/r2.speaker: Q, Z
STUDYQURAN:36:39/r2.claim: Q and Z explain the old palm stalk as the withered remains of a date cluster, resembling a thin crescent in shape, width, and color.
STUDYQURAN:36:39/r2.anchor: the thin crescent moon in shape, width, and color (Q, Z)

TABATABAI:36:38-39/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:38-39/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:38-39/r8.claim: Manāzil is plural of manzil, a place of descent; it likely denotes the moon’s twenty-eight stations, traversed in approximately twenty-eight days and nights.
TABATABAI:36:38-39/r8.anchor: المنازل جمع منزل اسم مكان من النزول والظاهر أن المراد به المنازل الثمانية والعشرون التي تقطعها القمر في كل ثمانية وعشرين يوما وليلة تقريبا

TABATABAI:36:38-39/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:38-39/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:38-39/r9.claim: The ʿurjūn is the curved yellow stalk of a date cluster, resembling a crescent; qadīm means old or aged.
TABATABAI:36:38-39/r9.anchor: والعرجون عود عذق النخلة من بين الشمراخ إلى منبته وهو عود أصفر مقوس يشبه الهلال، والقديم العتيق

TABATABAI:36:38-39/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:38-39/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:38-39/r10.claim: Among differing syntactic analyses, the clearest supplies ‘possessing stations’ or ‘stations for it’: God ordained the moon’s stations until it becomes a crescent like the old yellow stalk.
TABATABAI:36:38-39/r10.anchor: وأقرب التقديرات من الفهم قول من قال إن التقدير والقمر قدرناه ذا منازل أو قدرنا له منازل حتى عاد هلالا يشبه العرجون العتيق

TABATABAI:36:38-39/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:38-39/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:38-39/r11.claim: The verse describes changing lunar appearances relative to Earth: sunlight illuminates about half the moon, and as its position changes the visible crescent grows full, wanes, and returns to its beginning.
TABATABAI:36:38-39/r11.anchor: تشير الآية إلى اختلاف مناظر القمر بالنسبة إلى أهل الأرض فإن نوره مكتسب من الشمس يستنير بها نصف كرته تقريبا

TABATABAI:36:38-39/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:38-39/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:38-39/r12.claim: The moon’s changing forms have evident effects on land, sea, and human life; the verse addresses its states relative to Earth’s inhabitants, not its intrinsic state or only its relation to the sun.
TABATABAI:36:38-39/r12.anchor: ولاختلاف صوره آثار بارزة في البر والبحر وحياة الناس

TABATABAI:36:33-47#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:33-47#2/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:36:33-47#2/r3.claim: Salām ibn al-Mustanīr transmits from Abū Jaʿfar that God created the sun before the moon and light before darkness.
TABATABAI:36:33-47#2/r3.anchor: وفي روضة الكافي بإسناده عن سلام بن المستنير عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال إن الله عز وجل خلق الشمس قبل القمر

TABRISI:36:37-39/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:37-39/r2.speaker: أهل الحجاز والبصرة
TABRISI:36:37-39/r2.claim: Readers of the Hijaz and Basra, except Abu Jaʿfar and Ruways, read al-qamar in the nominative; the others read it in the accusative.
TABRISI:36:37-39/r2.anchor: وقرأ أهل الحجاز والبصرة غير أبي جعفر ورويس والقمر بالرفع والباقون بالنصب

TABRISI:36:37-39/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:37-39/r4.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:36:37-39/r4.claim: Abu ʿAli explains nominative al-qamar as a new sign parallel to “the night is a sign”; the clauses that follow explain the sign, as an explanatory clause may explain a promise or instruction.
TABRISI:36:37-39/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي الرفع على تقدير

TABRISI:36:37-39/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:37-39/r5.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:36:37-39/r5.claim: On this nominative analysis, ayatun is an indefinite subject, lahum modifies it, and an understood predicate is “in sight” or “in existence.”
TABRISI:36:37-39/r5.anchor: والقول في آية أنه يرتفع بالابتداء ولهم صفة للنكرة والخبر مضمر

TABRISI:36:37-39/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:37-39/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:37-39/r6.claim: The accusative reading links the moon to an object-fronted construction such as “Zaydan I struck.”
TABRISI:36:37-39/r6.anchor: ومن نصب فقد حمله على زيدا ضربته

TABRISI:36:37-39/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:37-39/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:37-39/r10.claim: The ʿurjun is the cluster bearing the date-palm’s branchlets, also called ʿuthkul, ʿithkal, kabasa, or qinw; the word is on the faʿlul pattern.
TABRISI:36:37-39/r10.anchor: والعرجون العذق الذي فيه الشماريخ وهو العثكول والعثكال والكباسة والقنو

TABRISI:36:37-39/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:37-39/r11.speaker: رؤبة
TABRISI:36:37-39/r11.claim: Ruʾba’s verse uses muʿarjan in describing a graceful, curved form, cited for the word ʿurjun.
TABRISI:36:37-39/r11.anchor: قال رؤبة: في خدر مياس الدمى معرجن

TABRISI:36:37-39/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:37-39/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:37-39/r12.claim: Manazil is understood as “possessor of stations,” with the noun deleted and its genitive substitute promoted; the moon is not stations but moves through them.
TABRISI:36:37-39/r12.anchor: تقديره ذا منازل ثم حذف المضاف وأقيم المضاف إليه مقامه

TABRISI:36:37-39/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:37-39/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:37-39/r13.claim: Manazil cannot be a direct locative because it is bounded; a verb takes a bounded place through a preposition, as “I sat in the mosque,” not “I sat the mosque.”
TABRISI:36:37-39/r13.anchor: ولا يجوز أن ينصب منازل على الظرف لأنه محدود والفعل لا يصل إلى المحدود

TABRISI:36:37-40/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:37-40/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:37-40/r8.claim: The moon has 28 stations, moving through one each day and night without variation until it traverses its orbit.
TABRISI:36:37-40/r8.anchor: وهي ثمانية وعشرون منزلا ينزل كل يوم وليلة منزلة منها لا يختلف حاله

TABRISI:36:37-40/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:37-40/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:37-40/r9.claim: At month’s end the moon becomes thin like an old, dry, curved date stalk, then disappears for two days; an old cluster dries and curves in the same way.
TABRISI:36:37-40/r9.anchor: أي عاد في آخر الشهر دقيقا كالعذق اليابس العتيق ثم يخفى يومين آخر الشهر

TABRISI:36:37-40/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:37-40/r10.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:36:37-40/r10.claim: Another view says the date cluster takes this dry, curved form every six months.
TABRISI:36:37-40/r10.anchor: وقيل: إن العذق يصير كذلك في كل ستة أشهر

TABRISI:36:37-40/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:37-40/r11.speaker: أبو الحسن الرضا
TABRISI:36:37-40/r11.claim: In a disputation with the Waqifi Abu Saʿid al-Makkari, al-Rida used the Jesus-Mary relation to explain his unity with his father, then ruled that ownership for six months counts as qadim in a deathbed manumission clause; Abu Saʿid later lost his sight and begged until death.
TABRISI:36:37-40/r11.anchor: دخل أبو سعيد المكاري وكان واقفيا على أبي الحسن الرضا ع فقال له أبلغ من قدرك

TABRISI:36:37-40/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:37-40/r12.speaker: أبو الحسن الرضا
TABRISI:36:37-40/r12.claim: Al-Rida rules that “old” property in a deathbed declaration freeing all old slaves includes anyone the owner has possessed for six months.
TABRISI:36:37-40/r12.anchor: قال أبو الحسن: ما ملكه لستة أشهر فهو قديم وهو حر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r1.claim: Al-qamar is read in both the nominative and accusative, with several syntactic analyses for each case.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق وأبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r2.claim: The nominative can estimate “and a sign for them is the moon,” as with the night and sun passages, or treat the moon as subject and qaddarnāhu as its predicate.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r2.anchor: فالرفع بتقدير: وآية لهم القمر، كما ذكرنا في قوله: {الليل نسلخ} و {والشمس تجري}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق وأبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r3.claim: The accusative can treat the phrase as “We measured the moon; We measured it,” like Sibawayh’s Arabic example “Zaydan aḍribtuhu.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r3.anchor: والنصب على: وقدرنا القمر قدرناه، وقد حمله سيبويه على: زيدا أضربته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ prefers the nominative: after calling the night a sign, the verse makes the sun and moon follow it as two further signs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء: في القمر (¬4) أعجب إلى؛ لأنه قال: {وآية لهم الليل} ثم جعل الشمس والقمر متبعين الليل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayda prefers the accusative because it is flanked by the preceding verb naslakh and following qaddarnāhu; he understands “We made it with stations,” omitting a noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: النصب أحب إلي؛ للفعل المتقدم قبله والمتأخر بعده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r6.claim: The moon’s stations are the familiar twenty-eight positions from the start of the month through its twenty-eighth night; at its final station it dwindles.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p484#2/r6.anchor: ومنازل القمر معروفة، وهي: ثمانية وعشرون منزلة، من أول الشهر إلى ثمان وعشرين ليلة منه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r1.claim: Abū Isḥāq says al-ʿurjūn is the stem supporting the small branches of a date cluster; when old and dry it becomes thin and small, like the moon at month’s end or first crescent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (العرجون عود العذق الذي تركبه الشماريخ من العذق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r2.claim: Abū Isḥāq derives ʿurjūn from the triliteral root ʿ-r-j and says an old date stem bends and becomes crooked.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r2.anchor: والعرجون على ما ذكر أبو إسحاق من الثلاثي؛ لأنه (¬4) جعل النون زائدة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r3.claim: The wording compresses the idea that the moon travels through its stations until it returns to the shape of an old date stem; mentioning stations implies its passage through them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r3.anchor: والآية مختصرة؛ لأن التقدير: فسار في منازله حتى عاد كالعرجون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī compares it to a dry date stem that has aged through a year and become crooked.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: كالعرجون اليابس قد حال عليه الحول فتوش

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r5.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r5.claim: Muqātil gives a similar explanation of the dry, aged date stem.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r6.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r6.claim: Al-Layth treats ʿurjūn as a quadriliteral: the base of the date cluster, broad and yellow, resembles the moon when it has dwindled; ʿarjana means depicting date stems.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r6.anchor: وذكره الليث في باب الرباعي فقال: العرجون أصل العذق، وهو أصفر عريض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r7.speaker: رؤبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r7.claim: Ruʾba’s phrase muʿarjan witnesses the sense of something depicted in the shape of palm clusters.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p485/r7.anchor: وقال رؤبة: في خدر مياس الدجى معرجن

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:35-41/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:35-41/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:35-41/r7.claim: At its last phase the moon resembles an old, dried, curved date-cluster stalk.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:35-41/r7.anchor: ذا منازل { حتى عاد } في آخر منزله { كالعرجون القديم } وهو عود الشمراخ إذا يبس اعوج

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p808/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p808/r1.speaker: الكلبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p808/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says the moon waxes and wanes as it proceeds through its stations.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p808/r1.anchor: والقمر قدرناه منازل} [يس: 38-39] يزيد وينقص في تفسير الكلبي، يجري على منازله.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p808/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p808/r2.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p808/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the moon never rises or sets except while increasing or decreasing.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p808/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن: لا يطلع ولا يغيب إلا في زيادة أو نقصان.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p808/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p808/r3.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p808/r3.claim: Mujahid compares the moon to a dried palm stalk’s neck when it is a crescent.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p808/r3.anchor: المعلى، عن ابن يحيى، عن مجاهد، قال: كعنق النخلة اليابس، يعني: إذا كان هلالا.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p192/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p192/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p192/r4.claim: The moon descends one station each night; it has twenty-eight stations from the month’s start through night twenty-eight, then disappears.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p192/r4.anchor: يريد: أنه ينزل كل ليلة منزلا، ومنازله ثمانية وعشرون منزلا عندهم، من أول الشهر إلى ثمان وعشرين ليلة منه ثم يستسر.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p192/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p192/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p192/r5.claim: The 28 stations are الشرطان، البطين، الثريا، الدبران، الهقعة، الهنعة، الذراع، النثرة، الطرف، الجبهة، الزبرة، الصرفة، العواء، السماك، الغفر، الزباني، الإكليل، القلب، الشولة، النعائم، البلدة، سعد الذابح، سعد بلع، سعد السعود، سعد الأخبية، فرغ الدلو المقدم، فرغ الدلو المؤخر، الرشا (الحوت); Arabs linked these stars to anwaʾ.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p192/r5.anchor: وهذه المنازل هي النجوم التي كانت العرب تنسب إليها الأنواء.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p192/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p192/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p192/r6.claim: At its last station the moon thins like an old dried palm cluster, which dries, narrows, and curves like a bow; this is its form on night twenty-eight.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p192/r6.anchor: وإذا صار القمر في آخر منازله دق حتى يعود كالعرجون القديم وهو العذق اليابس.

ELMALILI:36:39-40/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:39-40/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:39-40/r1.claim: Unlike the steadily moving Sun, the Moon has appointed stations and measures, reaching one station each day and appearing in a different form at each.
ELMALILI:36:39-40/r1.anchor: O Güneş gibi istikrarlı bir surette cereyan etmez. Ona birtakım menziller ve her menzile göre bir mikdar tâyin etmişizdir.

ELMALILI:36:39-40/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:39-40/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:39-40/r2.claim: Elmalılı lists the Arab lunar mansions: Şertan, butayn, süreyya, deberan, hek‘a, hen‘a, zira‘, nesre, tarf, cebhe, zübre, sarfe, avvâ’, simâk, gafr, zubânâ, iklil, kalb, şevle, ne‘âim, belde, sa‘dü’zzâbih, sa‘dü büla‘, sa‘du’s-su‘ûd, sa‘du’l-ahbiye, fer‘u’d-delvi’l-mukaddem, fer‘u’d-delvi’l-muahhar, reşâ.
ELMALILI:36:39-40/r2.anchor: Araplar, menâzil-i Kamer’i şunlarla saymışlardı[^1]: Şertan[^2], butayn, süreyya

ELMALILI:36:39-40/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:39-40/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:39-40/r3.claim: The Moon passes one mansion nightly, waxing toward fullness and then waning until it is very thin and crescent-shaped in its final station before conjunction.
ELMALILI:36:39-40/r3.anchor: Bunlardan her gece bir menzile konar da istikbâle kadar günden güne nûru arta arta sonra da eksile eksile son menzilde

ELMALILI:36:39-40/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:39-40/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:39-40/r4.claim: An “urjūn” is a curved stalk, especially the base of a date cluster; an old one is thinner, more curved, and more colored.
ELMALILI:36:39-40/r4.anchor: “Urcûn” eğri salkım çöpü demektir. Bilhassa hurma salkımının dip çöpü ki eskisi, yani geçen seneninki daha ince, daha eğri, daha renkli olur.

ELMALILI:36:39-40/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:39-40/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:39-40/r5.claim: The simile does more than depict the crescent’s first and last shapes: it also sketches the Moon’s path around Earth over a month.
ELMALILI:36:39-40/r5.anchor: Bu teşbih pek bedî‘dir. Zannedildiği gibi hilâlin ilk ve son şeklini göstermekle kalmıyor, Kamer’in o menâzilde giderken Arz etrafında bir ayda

ELMALILI:36:39-40/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:39-40/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:39-40/r6.claim: Calling the stalk old imagines the Moon’s body at each station along its path; ancient astronomers did not grasp the subtlety of this comparison.
ELMALILI:36:39-40/r6.anchor: “Eski” denilmekle bu mahrek üzerinde Kamer’in her menzildeki cirmi de tahyîl edilmiş bulunuyor ki eski heyetçiler bu teşbihin letâfetini idrak edemezlerdi.

MAJAZ:v2p161/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p161/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p161/r2.claim: The old crescent is compared to the ihān, the palm-stalk at whose top are the fruit clusters and their branchlets; ʿidhq with fatḥa means a palm tree.
MAJAZ:v2p161/r2.anchor: هو الإهان إهان العذق الذي فى أعلاه العثاكيل وهى الشماريخ والعذق بفتح العين النخلة

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r3.claim: The Moon reflects a small fraction of sunlight, illuminates Earth at night, and, with the Sun, has a special role in timekeeping and calendars.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r3.anchor: güneşten aldığı ışığın çok az bir kısmını dünyaya göndermekte, böylece –evrelerine göre farklılık taşımakla beraber– geceleri açık havada yeryüzünü aydınlatmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r4.claim: Their visibility and importance to human life have long attracted attention and shaped religious beliefs, even to the point of deifying them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r4.anchor: güneş ve ay öteden beri insanların ilgisini celbetmiş, hatta –tanrılaştırma düzeyine varacak kadar– dinî inançları etkilemiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r33.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r33.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r33.claim: Manāzil, the plural of manzil, means a place where one alights or a stopping place.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r33.anchor: menâzilin tekili olan menzil kelimesinin sözlük anlamı “inilecek yer, durak”tır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r34.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r34.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r34.claim: As the Moon travels around Earth, its sunlit face visibly changes from day to day; Arab astronomers named 28 stations, each corresponding to a daily path of about thirteen degrees, while the Moon is unseen for one or two nights in a 29- or 30-day month.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r34.anchor: Ayın gökyüzündeki hareketi için, her biri bir günlük yola karşılık gelmek üzere 13’er derecelik yaylardan oluşan 28 menzil tesbit edilmiş olup Araplar bu menzillere ayrı ayrı isimler vermişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r35.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r35.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r35.claim: The verse may also refer to lunar phases, which result from the Moon’s position relative to Earth and Sun and are commonly named new moon, first quarter, full moon, and last quarter.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r35.anchor: bu periyodik olayın yaklaşık birer haftalık sürelere göre incelenmesi neticesinde ayın dünyadan değişik görünümlerine ayın safhaları (evreleri) denmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r36.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r36.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r36.claim: Urcūn is the stalk left on a date palm after its fruit cluster is cut; when old, it becomes thin, curved, and yellow, features compared to the Moon.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r36.anchor: “Urcûn” kelimesi hurma salkımı kesildikten sonra bu salkımın ağaçta kalan sapını ifade eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r37.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r37.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r37.claim: Because qadīm describes such objects after at least a year, the translation renders it “years old.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r37.anchor: bu tür nesneler için üzerinden en az bir yıl geçme durumlarında kullanıldığı için

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r38.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r38.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r38.claim: Rāzī notes that the adjective is not necessarily restricted to objects over a year old.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r38.anchor: Râzî, XXVI, 72-73; bunu “kuru” şeklinde ifade etmek de mümkündür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r39.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r39.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:38/r39.claim: Tabarī allows translating qadīm here as “dry.”

BAQILLANI:v1p187/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p187/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p187/r3.claim: Every Qur'anic word can carry complete eloquence on its own, yet gains further beauty and instruction in composition; these verses exceed familiar speech and human ability.
BAQILLANI:v1p187/r3.anchor: فإذا كانت الآية تنتظم من البديع وتتألف من البلاغات فكيف لا تفوت حد المعهود ولا تحوز شأو المألوف

BURHAN:v3p215/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p215/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p215/r2.claim: We determined the moon means We determined for it, with the preposition understood.

ITQAN:v2p327#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p327#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p327#2/r2.claim: The old ʿurjūn is the aged base of a date cluster.

NAHHAS:v3p393/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p393/r11.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v3p393/r11.claim: The Kufians read والقمر accusative with an implied verb; Abu Ubayd prefers this because verbs precede and follow it.
NAHHAS:v3p393/r11.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون ( والقمر ) بالنصب على إضمار فعل وهو اختيار أبي عبيد

NAHHAS:v3p393/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p393/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p393/r12.claim: Al-Nahhas prefers the nominative with the preceding nominative and والشمس; he says grammarians, including al-Farra, oppose Abu Ubayd's argument.
NAHHAS:v3p393/r12.anchor: أهل العربية جميعا فيما علمت على خلاف ما قال منهم الفراء قال الرفع أعجب إلي

NAHHAS:v3p393/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p393/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p393/r13.claim: The nominative may make القمر a subject; for قدرناه منازل, supply ذا before منازل or understand قدرنا له منازل with the preposition omitted.
NAHHAS:v3p393/r13.anchor: ويقال القمر ليس هو المنازل فكيف قال قدرنا منازل ففي هذا جوابان أحدهما أن تقديره قدرناه ذا منازل

ITQAN:v3p115/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p115/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p115/r2.claim: The moon’s resemblance to an old date stalk and the people like uprooted palm trunks exemplify comparison between two sensory things.
ITQAN:v3p115/r2.anchor: ﴿ والقمر قدرناه منازل حتى عاد كالعرجون القديم ﴾ ﴿ كأنهم أعجاز نخل منقعر ﴾

NASHR:v2p353/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p353/r8.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وروح
NASHR:v2p353/r8.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, and Rawḥ read the rāʾ in qaddarnāhu with ḍamma; the others read it with fatḥa.
NASHR:v2p353/r8.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وروح برفع الراء
